hello.note: From Australian English 'g'day'; friendly and all-purpose.

good_morning.note: Simple English loanword, used the same way.

good_evening.note: Literally 'afternoon'; used loosely from midday into evening since Tok Pisin has no separate 'good evening' term.

how_are_you.note: Literally 'you stay well?'; reply with 'Mi orait.'

thank_you.note: Add 'tru' (Tenkyu tru) to mean 'thank you very much.'

youre_welcome.note: Literally 'no problem/nothing'; the standard reply to thanks. 'Nogat wari' (no worries) also works.

slang.note: Playful, drawn-out 'don't you worry'; said with extra warmth/attitude among friends, more animated than the plain reply.

no_problem.note: Casual 'never mind, no worries'; brushes off thanks or a small mistake as nothing.

excuse_me.note: From English 'excuse'; used to pass by or get attention.

yes.note: 'Ya' is also common and slightly more casual.

of_course.note: Adds 'tru' (truly) to a plain yes for emphasis, close to 'of course/definitely.'

amazing.note: Literally 'number one'; the standard word for 'the best.'

delicious.note: From English 'sweet'; used for any good-tasting food.

cheers.note: Said as-is from English; Tok Pisin has no distinct native toast. 'God blesim yu' (God bless you) is also heard when raising a glass.
